_note: Shot lists for the 25-episode Hoodlum Soldier AI series, adapted from Elvin's screenplay episodes. t=talk: characters say the line on camera (lip-synced, generated with audio). t=vo: Ali's older narrator voice over the shot. t=act: picture and sound only. c=cast ids in frame (first = main subject). g=grade from cast.json. s for talk uses 'id: line | id: line'. d=seconds. loc=location super typed on screen.

shots.v: slow push down a cracked empty Newark street at night, a streetlight flickering, a skinny stray pitbull limps across the wet pavement, distant sirens
red and blue police lights pulse at the far end of a dark block of rowhouses, a man on a stoop doesn't even look up, distant gunshots echo
inside a parked old Cutlass Supreme at night, the teenager sits low in the driver seat, hood up, jaw clenched, streetlight sliding across his face, slow push in
extreme close up of his trembling fingers resting near a snub-nose revolver on his lap in the dark car, then his eyes in the rearview mirror

shots.s: Seventeen. And I already thought I knew how my story ended.
shots.v: the teenager steps out of the car and crosses the street toward a rundown trap house, hood up, tracking shot from behind

shots.s: girl: You my brother Dre's friend? | ali_teen: Used to be.
shots.v: a small girl sits on porch steps under a bare bulb holding a headless doll, she looks up at the hooded teenager standing at the bottom of the steps, he answers quietly
his fist knocks twice on a battered door, a long tense silence, then red and blue police lights suddenly flood the whole porch and his face
a courtroom, the teenager in an orange jumpsuit and handcuffs stands at the defense table, behind him in the gallery his mother sobs quietly into her hands

shots.s: judge: You got two options, son. Prison. Or the United States Army. You choose.
shots.v: the judge leans forward over the bench in a wood-paneled courtroom, window light, speaking directly down to the defendant
close up of the teenager in the orange jumpsuit, he looks down, then slowly lifts his eyes to the judge, and nods once

shots.s: That nod was the first real choice I ever made.
shots.v: slow push in on a folded American flag resting beside a red bandana on a wooden table, dust in a shaft of light
dawn heat, an army bus pulls up on a training base, the door hisses and creaks open, low angle

shots.s: mack: Welcome to the United States Army! Y'all think this is a game? Y'all mine now!
shots.v: the drill sergeant storms the bus door screaming at recruits, spit flying, low angle, recruits scrambling off behind him
the recruit steps off the bus last with a duffel bag, unsure but determined, recruits scrambling into formation around him, handheld

shots.s: This ain't redemption. It's war. And war don't care where you from.
shots.v: wide shot of rows of recruits standing at attention on a parade field under a hard white sky, flag snapping
night in a dark barracks, the recruit lies awake on a bottom bunk staring at the ceiling, a distant marching cadence echoes

shots.s: roddy: Yo. You from Jersey? I'm Roddy. Kentucky. | ali_recruit: Yeah. Newark.
shots.v: the freckled recruit leans over from the next bunk in the moonlit barracks whispering with a grin, the other recruit turns his head toward him

shots.s: roddy: Bet y'all got good pizza. And bad cops. | ali_recruit: Facts.
shots.v: both recruits laughing quietly on their bunks in the dark so the drill sergeant won't hear, the first smile on his face

shots.s: Didn't know it then. But that bunk was my first taste of brotherhood.
shots.v: two pairs of boots side by side under neighboring bunks, moonlight through a barracks window, slow dolly
dog tags swaying gently from a bunk rail in the moonlight
recruits crawling on their bellies under barbed wire through deep mud, the recruit pushes through, mud on his face, rain falling, low ground-level camera
the drill sergeant walks up and stands over the muddy recruit on his knees, rain dripping off the campaign hat

shots.s: mack: You think the streets made you tough? The enemy don't care where you from. You fight for the man next to you. Got it?
shots.v: close up, the drill sergeant leans down nose to nose in the rain, intense

shots.s: ali_recruit: Got it, Sergeant. | mack: Then show me.
shots.v: the recruit covered in mud stares back and answers, the drill sergeant straightens up

shots.s: Every step in that mud, I was stepping further from who I used to be.
shots.v: the recruit pushes to his feet with his rifle and charges forward through the mud, slow motion boots splashing
night, the recruit sits alone on his bunk in a dark barracks, headphones in, phone glowing on his face

shots.s: mom (voicemail, off screen): Baby boy, just checking in. I know you're doing good. I'm proud of you.
shots.v: close on the recruit's face lit by the phone as a woman's warm voice plays through the voicemail, his eyes well up
extreme close up of his thumb pressing delete on the voicemail, the screen goes dark

shots.s: It hurt too much to hear love when I didn't feel it for myself.
shots.v: the recruit sits in silence in the dark barracks, head down, slow push in

shots.s: mack: Know the terrain. Know your brothers. Don't rely on luck. Rely on instinct. Your life depends on how well you listen today.
shots.v: the drill sergeant walks between rows of desks in an army classroom, tactics diagrams on a screen behind him
the recruit writing notes furiously in a notebook, completely locked in

shots.s: I used to zone out in school. But war ain't got no make-up test.
shots.v: a notebook full of handwritten notes and diagrams, a pencil pressing hard
the recruit prone on a firing line, calm breath, rifle cracks, a distant target pops with tight hits, shell casings flying

shots.s: flores: Damn, Jersey. You got that assassin vibe. | ali_recruit: Just blockin' out the noise.
shots.v: the female soldier kneels beside him on the range grinning, he answers without looking up from his rifle

shots.s: doc: That's why you dangerous. Calm outside. Chaos inside.
shots.v: the stocky medic leans on a range barrier laughing, pointing at the shooter
a crowded army chow hall, the tall soldier tells a story with big hand gestures, the female soldier mimics a drill sergeant, the whole table erupts in laughter, the recruit actually smiles

shots.s: In that mess hall, I found more family than I ever had back home.
shots.v: wide warm shot of a long table of soldiers eating and laughing together
evening in a base mail room, the soldier tears open an envelope, a child's crayon drawing slides out with a handwritten letter
close up of a child's crayon drawing of a little house and a stick soldier holding hands with a little girl

shots.s: mom: We miss you. Keep your head up. Don't forget who you are.
shots.v: a memory: his mother at her kitchen table writing a letter by lamplight, speaking the words softly as she writes
the soldier stares at the drawing, a tear forms, he quickly wipes it and hides it

shots.s: roddy: That your girl? | ali_recruit: Nah. That's my lil' sister. She the only one still innocent.
shots.v: the freckled soldier leans over on the bench to look at the drawing, the other soldier answers quietly holding it
he folds the letter and drawing carefully and slides it into his uniform chest pocket, pats it twice
a C-17 cargo plane on a runway at dusk, soldiers with rucksacks marching up the ramp into the belly of the plane

shots.s: I carried that drawing everywhere. It was the only part of me still clean.
shots.v: a folded letter tucked behind dog tags on a cot as the plane engines roar
a squad moving through a narrow dusty alley, weapons up, heat haze, handheld, tense silence

shots.s: flores: Movement on the roof!
shots.v: the female soldier in helmet snaps her rifle up toward a rooftop and shouts
gunfire erupts, dust kicking up, the soldier dives behind a parked vehicle and returns fire, chaos and smoke, shaky camera

shots.s: q: Stay low! | doc: I'm hit! I'm hit!
shots.v: the tall soldier shouting while crouched in smoke, the medic falls clutching his leg behind him
the soldier sprints out, grabs the wounded medic by the vest and drags him behind cover through flying dust

shots.s: This wasn't a movie. This was blood. Real. And everywhere.
shots.v: aftermath, a dusty helmet lying alone in a silent alley, smoke drifting
night inside an army tent, lantern light, soldiers sitting silently, one writes a letter, one stares at nothing

shots.s: roddy: You saved Doc's life, man. | ali_soldier: He would've done it for me.
shots.v: the freckled soldier sits down beside him on a cot, the other keeps cleaning his rifle and answers without looking up

shots.s: For the first time, I wasn't just surviving. I was protecting. I mattered.
shots.v: desert stars over a military camp, slow tilt up
night, the soldier on watch at a desert base gate, wind howling sand across the spotlight beam
a small local boy about ten walks slowly toward the gate in the dark holding a round object against his chest

shots.s: flores: Ali! That kid's not allowed in the zone!
shots.v: the female soldier shouts from the guard tower, spotlight swinging
close up, the soldier raises his rifle and aims, breath held, sweat on his face
the boy drops the object, it rolls into the spotlight, it's just a worn soccer ball
the soldier slowly lowers his rifle and bows his head, shaken

shots.s: We were trained to see threats. Even in the innocent.
shots.v: the empty gate at night, the soccer ball sitting alone in the sand
a makeshift tent chapel, the soldier lights a single candle, he doesn't pray, just stares at the flame

shots.s: chaplain: You don't gotta believe in God. Just believe you ain't alone. That's harder.
shots.v: the chaplain sits down on the bench beside him in candlelight and speaks gently

shots.s: I wasn't religious. But I was desperate.
shots.v: a candle flame flickering in the dark, extreme close up
the soldier on his bunk in a desert barracks opens a letter, a gold star sticker on the page

shots.s: sister: I made honor roll! I hope you come home soon. Mommy says you're a hero.
shots.v: a memory: his little sister at her kitchen table proudly holding up a report card and talking to the camera
the soldier smiles and leans back against the wall, eyes closed, the letter resting on his chest

shots.s: I was fighting more for her now than myself.
shots.v: he tucks the letter into his helmet band
night, two soldiers sit on top of the base wall with their legs hanging over the ledge, base lights below and stars above, from behind

shots.s: q: I enlisted to pay off my grandma's house. Thought I'd do four and bounce. | ali_soldier: I ran from a jail cell.
shots.v: the two soldiers talking quietly on the wall at night, profile shot, faces lit by distant base lights

shots.s: q: And now? | ali_soldier: Now I just wanna live long enough to fix what I broke.
shots.v: close on the soldier as he answers, looking out at the desert
dawn breaking over the desert from the base wall, razor wire in silhouette
a convoy of Humvees rolling down a dusty road, heat haze, drone shot

shots.s: roddy: Why this road always feel cursed?
shots.v: inside a Humvee, the freckled soldier in helmet looks out the window and mutters, tension
a massive roadside IED blast engulfs a Humvee in fire and dust, shockwave, debris
the soldier wakes up dazed upside down in smoke, blood on his forehead, muffled ringing

shots.s: q: We got casualties! We got casualties!
shots.v: the tall soldier shouting into a radio in the smoke beside the wreck
the soldier crawls out of the wreckage into the dust, dazed but alive

shots.s: flores: That's your second close call. | ali_soldier: Death don't want me yet. | doc: You too stubborn.
shots.v: a field medical tent, the bandaged soldier on a cot, his squad standing around him, a tired joke

shots.s: doctor (off screen): Trouble sleeping? Flashbacks? | ali_soldier: Only when I close my eyes.
shots.v: a stark psych evaluation office under fluorescent light, the soldier sits across a desk and answers flatly

shots.s: They knew it. And sent us back anyway.
shots.v: the soldier walks back toward the trucks alone, seen from behind, dusk
an alarm blares, distant gunfire, the soldier straps on body armor fast with steady hands, quick cuts

shots.s: The scariest part of war? Ain't the bullets. It's how normal it starts to feel.
shots.v: an empty cot with a helmet resting on it, slow push
a calm dusk patrol, soldiers walking and joking, the freckled soldier laughing and throwing a playful punch
the soldier walks rear security at the back of the patrol, watching the rooftops
a sudden blinding explosion of dust and fire at dusk, everyone thrown to the ground
ears ringing, dust settling, the soldier lifts his head from the ground and looks over, a fallen soldier lies motionless

shots.s: ali_soldier: Roddy! Roddy! Come on, man!
shots.v: the soldier crawls through the dust to his fallen friend screaming his name, shaking him

shots.s: mack: Move, soldier! We're under attack!
shots.v: the sergeant in combat gear grabs him by the vest and drags him toward cover through smoke

shots.s: And just like that, he was gone. Smiling one second. Gone the next.
shots.v: an empty helmet lying in the sand as smoke drifts across the sunset
a helicopter pad, soldiers stand in silence around a flag-draped body bag being loaded, rotor wind whipping sand

shots.s: mack: He gave everything. And we honor that by finishing the fight.
shots.v: the sergeant standing at attention addressing the squad, voice tight
the soldier wipes a tear with his gloved hand and stands straight, composed

shots.s: You don't bury your past in a coffin. You carry it.
shots.v: the helicopter lifts off into a hazy amber sky
night inside a military transport plane, the soldier stares out the small window at the clouds, red cabin light
extreme close up of his hand opening to reveal a pair of dog tags stamped RODDY

shots.s: I went to war a hoodlum. And came back haunted.
shots.v: clouds below the plane wing in moonlight
a nearly empty bus station at night, cold breath in the air, no welcome party, the veteran stands alone with a duffel bag
he pulls the duffel over his shoulder and walks into the dark Newark streets, seen from behind

shots.s: Home didn't feel like home anymore. And I didn't feel like me anymore.
shots.v: a quiet Newark rowhouse street at night, one window lit

shots.s: mom: You look older. | ali_vet: I feel it.
shots.v: his mother stands frozen in the kitchen doorway staring at him, warm lamp light, he stands in the hall
she rushes to him and hugs him tight in the small kitchen, he breaks down in her arms

shots.s: I ain't cry in combat. But I did cry in her arms.
shots.v: the kitchen at night, two figures embracing in silhouette
his old teenage bedroom, faded posters, creaky bed, he hangs dog tags on a nail and looks into the mirror, not recognizing himself

shots.s: The boy that left this room never came back.
shots.v: an empty bed in a dim bedroom, streetlight through the blinds
a crowded VA office, fluorescent lights, long lines, paperwork, the veteran waits holding a folder

shots.s: clerk (off screen): You're not in our system yet. Could take a few months. | ali_vet: Months? I need help now.
shots.v: the veteran at a service counter, a clerk's hand stamps a form, his face tightens with frustration

shots.s: clerk (off screen): Everyone does, sir. Next.
shots.v: the veteran stares, then slowly steps aside as the line moves forward

shots.s: The war ain't over when you come home. It just change uniforms.
shots.v: the veteran walks out of the office into grey daylight
night, the kitchen, the veteran eats cereal with his little sister at the table, she looks up at him

shots.s: sister: Are you okay now? | ali_vet: Yeah. Just tired.
shots.v: close two shot at the kitchen table, she asks softly, he forces a small smile

shots.s: sister: Don't worry. I'll be strong for both of us.
shots.v: the girl puts her small hand on top of his big hand on the table

shots.s: She grew up while I was gone. But kept my heart safe.
shots.v: the kitchen light glowing in a dark house, her crayon drawing on the fridge

shots.s: dre: Yo! My man back from the sandbox!
shots.v: daylight on a Newark street corner, the young man in a puffer jacket spots him and comes in for a dap and hug

shots.s: ali_vet: I'm not that dude no more. | dre: You still from here. Never forget that.
shots.v: the two men face each other on the corner, tension under the smiles

shots.s: He was right. But that didn't mean I had to stay stuck here.
shots.v: the veteran walks away from the corner, not looking back
nightmare flashes, fire and smoke, explosions, a soldier screaming in slow motion, dreamlike blur
the veteran jolts upright in bed in the dark, drenched in sweat, breathing hard
in a dark bathroom he splashes water on his face and stares at himself in the mirror

shots.s: Sleep used to be my escape. Now it's where the demons live.
shots.v: the bathroom mirror reflection in deep shadow, water dripping

shots.s: msjames: You've been through more than most. That changes people. That's okay.
shots.v: a therapy room with soft window light, the therapist speaks gently from her chair

shots.s: ali_vet: I don't need help. | msjames: Then why are you here?
shots.v: the veteran sits with arms crossed, distant, then he has no answer

shots.s: msjames: You can't fight your mind like it's Fallujah. You gotta surrender to healing.
shots.v: close on the therapist leaning forward, steady and kind

shots.s: I hated hearing that. But part of me knew she was right.
shots.v: the veteran looks down at his hands
an old boxing gym, the veteran pounds a heavy bag with fury, sweat flying, people glance over

shots.s: trainer: You fight? | ali_vet: I survived. | trainer: Same thing. You want a job?
shots.v: the old trainer steps up beside the heavy bag, the veteran catches his breath and answers

shots.s: I needed purpose. Even if it started with pain.
shots.v: dawn, the veteran wraps his hands alone in the quiet gym, one light over the ring

shots.s: ali_vet: We all wore the uniform. But none of us got the same salute coming home.
shots.v: a circle of veterans in a community room, the veteran speaks to the group

shots.s: vet (off screen): Preach that, Jersey.
shots.v: an older veteran's hand pats his back, the circle nods
a sunny park, the veteran plays catch with his little nephew, laughing for real

shots.s: Healing ain't a straight line. But moments like this? They matter.
shots.v: a baseball in the air against a bright sky, slow motion
night on Newark streets, a dealer on the corner nods at him, the veteran keeps walking

shots.s: kid (off screen): You was in the Army, right? That's crazy. You from here and made it out.
shots.v: a teenage boy calls out from across the street under a streetlight, the veteran pauses and turns
the veteran nods at the boy, a small proud nod

shots.s: Maybe I ain't a hero. But maybe I could be a mirror for the next kid.
shots.v: a reflection of the city street in a shop window at night

shots.s: ali_mentor: You ain't weak for crying. You strong for surviving.
shots.v: a school gym, kids on the bleachers, the man speaks into a microphone, kids hold up phones

shots.s: I stopped chasing validation and started giving back.
shots.v: the bleachers erupt in applause, warm light
a church, the man sits alone in the back pew, quiet

shots.s: pastor: God don't just call the qualified. He qualifies the called.
shots.v: the pastor at the pulpit looks right at the back pew, stained glass light

shots.s: I wasn't perfect. But I was chosen.
shots.v: the man bows his head in the pew, light streaming through stained glass
outside, the man helps neighborhood kids paint a huge colorful mural on a brick wall of a soldier in a hoodie

shots.s: kid (off screen): You really lived all that? | ali_mentor: Yeah. And I'm still living through it.
shots.v: a kid with a paintbrush looks up at him, he answers and they fist bump in front of the mural

shots.s: ali_mentor: We ain't crazy. We're scarred. And scars mean we survived.
shots.v: a radio studio, on-air light glowing red, the man speaks into a studio microphone with headphones on

shots.s: caller (on the line): Thank you, man. I needed this.
shots.v: phone lines lighting up on the studio board, he listens and nods
a school field, the man coaches kids playing flag football, shouting and celebrating a touchdown with them

shots.s: Joy found me when I stopped running from it.
shots.v: kids jumping and hugging their coach in golden light, slow motion
a bookstore, a long line of readers, the man signs copies of a book titled HOODLUM SOLDIER

shots.s: teen (off screen): This saved me, for real. | ali_mentor: Then it was worth it.
shots.v: a teenager holds the book tight to his chest at the table, the man looks up at him moved
a community center job fair, young veterans start forming a circle around the man

shots.s: When your story touches others, it ain't just yours anymore.
shots.v: hands reaching out for handshakes

shots.s: msjames: You've come a long way. Still got miles to go. | ali_mentor: True. But I'm not walking alone anymore.
shots.v: a sunny therapy room, the therapist, softer now, smiles at him, they shake hands
night, two teenage boys brawling in the street under a streetlight, the man pulls them apart

shots.s: ali_mentor: This how y'all wanna end up? Dead or in a cell?
shots.v: the man standing between the two boys, firm, pointing at both

shots.s: boy (off screen): You don't know our life! | ali_mentor: I am your life. I was you.
shots.v: close on the man as a boy shouts at him, he answers low and steady
the two boys freeze and lower their fists, silence, respect lingers under the streetlight

shots.s: host (off screen): From the battlefield to bestselling author. What would you tell the youth? | ali_mentor: Pain ain't permanent. But neither is peace. You gotta fight for both.
shots.v: a bright television studio couch, the man answers the host
a stark prison classroom, rows of inmates in tan uniforms, the man walks to the front

shots.s: ali_mentor: I had a record. I had nothing. But I used my pain as power. You ain't done, unless you say you are.
shots.v: the man speaking intensely at the front of the classroom
an inmate in the back row wipes a tear from his face
a candlelight vigil at night, mothers holding posters with photos of lost sons

shots.s: mother (off screen): Thank you for remembering our boys. | ali_mentor: They ain't forgotten. Not while I breathe.
shots.v: a grieving mother holding a candle speaks to him, he answers and lights his candle from hers
many candles glowing in the dark, the man bows his head

shots.s: ali_mentor: Even soldiers cry. And that's okay.
shots.v: the man sits reading his book to a classroom of fifth graders on a rug

shots.s: boy (off screen): Were you scared? | ali_mentor: Every day. But I showed up anyway.
shots.v: a small boy raises his hand, the man smiles and answers him

shots.s: vet (off screen): They all forgot me. | ali_mentor: Not me.
shots.v: a hospital parking lot at dusk, the man kneels to shake hands with a wounded veteran in a wheelchair

shots.s: Real soldiers never leave one behind. Even when the battle's over.
shots.v: the wheelchair silhouette against a sunset as he pushes it

shots.s: mom: You really here for good this time? | ali_mentor: Yeah, Ma. I'm home.
shots.v: a warm family dinner, his mother and grown sister laughing, glasses of iced tea clink
a memorial wall, his finger slowly traces an engraved name

shots.s: Some names live forever. Not 'cause they lived long. But 'cause they lived right.
shots.v: dog tags left hanging beside the name on the memorial wall at sunrise
a home office at night, war photos and a child's drawings on the wall, the man writes CHAPTER ONE in a notebook under a desk lamp

shots.s: We gotta own our pain. Or someone else will profit off it.
shots.v: a stack of handwritten pages under lamplight
a courtroom, the man sits holding hands with his young daughter

shots.s: judge: Mister Torres, you've shown growth and stability. Full visitation granted.
shots.v: the judge looks up from papers and speaks, window light

shots.s: Redemption looks a lot like responsibility.
shots.v: the man closes his eyes and exhales, his daughter hugs his arm
a grassy field at sunset, father and daughter run and fly a kite together

shots.s: daughter: I love when you're here, Daddy. | ali_mentor: I love being here, baby girl.
shots.v: the girl looks up at him holding the kite string, he kneels down to her

shots.s: She saved me. Without even knowing.
shots.v: the kite high in a golden sky

shots.s: ali_mentor: Y'all remind me of me. What saved me wasn't the Army. It was a decision.
shots.v: a fenced detention yard, teenage boys in orange jumpsuits, the man speaks to them

shots.s: boy (off screen): I wanna choose too.
shots.v: one boy in orange locks eyes with him, light on the fence
the old Newark corner at dusk, same stoop, kids wave and run up to greet him

shots.s: Legacy ain't what you leave. It's who you lift.
shots.v: the man walks down the block with kids around him
a cemetery, the man places a photo of himself in uniform against his father's headstone

shots.s: ali_mentor: I used to hate you for not being there. Now I just hope I did better.
shots.v: the man speaks quietly to the grave, then stands

shots.s: ali_mentor: If I could tell my seventeen year old self one thing? You ain't a mistake. You just ain't been molded yet.
shots.v: the man sits in front of a black backdrop, a single key light, speaking straight to camera like a documentary interview
his bedroom at night, the man kneels beside his bed in prayer for the first time, moonlight

shots.s: I didn't know what to say. But I knew what I needed. Peace.
shots.v: moonlight through the window over the kneeling silhouette
a church baptism, the pastor lowers the man into the water and helps him rise, water streaming off his face

shots.s: Rebirth ain't always easy. But it's always worth it.
shots.v: water drops falling through light, slow motion

shots.s: vet (off screen): I got nothin' left. | ali_mentor: You got breath. That's more than some had.
shots.v: a vet support group, the man hugs a broken young veteran tight

shots.s: doc: You still overcook chicken, bruh!
shots.v: a backyard barbecue, smoke rising, the stocky man and the tall man walk up laughing, older now, the host turns from the grill
the three old friends hug and laugh at the grill, kids running around at sunset

shots.s: We made it. Somehow. Some way.
shots.v: the grill glowing at dusk, laughter
a Jersey street, a mural of a smiling freckled soldier with the words HE GAVE ALL, the man touches the wall, hand over heart, keeps walking
another huge mural of a soldier in army gear and a hoodie with the words HOODLUM SOLDIER PROTECT YOUR PEACE, the man looks up at it
a cemetery, the man kneels at a grave with a folded flag and a photo of his old squad

shots.s: Some stories don't end happy. But they end honest. And sometimes that's enough.
shots.v: the man stands and salutes the grave, seen from behind

shots.s: daughter: You miss them? | ali_mentor: Every day. But I carry them in every step I take.
shots.v: a veterans memorial at sunset, father and daughter place flowers, she looks up at him
a city rooftop at sunset, the man stands calm and peaceful looking over the Newark skyline, seen from behind

shots.s: I fought wars in foreign lands. And in my own mind. But the real victory was choosing to heal.
shots.v: the sun setting over the skyline, slow aerial pull back
